item.title: Targeted advertising is also targeting malware

item.title: China announces new plans to take US industry head on
item.description: China has unveiled ambitious plans to compete with the US on emerging technologies by increasing funding for start-ups. The Chinese government said it wanted the digital economy to account for 12.5% of gross domestic product by 2030, a significant increase on the 10.5% share reported last year. item.description: GPT just keeps getting better at mathematics, increasingly solving the trickiest of problems. item.title: European consumers ask EU to put a stop to digital enshittification
item.description: Online rights campaigners have come together to complain about the propensity of IT companies to make life more difficult for their users. The groups, mainly from Europe but with some from the US, have written to policy makers in the EU/EEA, UK and the US. The initiative has been spearheaded by Forbrukerrådet (the Norwegian Consumer Council) which complained of the “enshittification” of software. item.title: Gov’t IT spending seen as key to building Europe’s tech ecosystem
item.description: As more European organizations reconsider their reliance on US technology suppliers amid rising geopolitical and trade tensions, public sector organizations are leading the way in a potential shift to local tech providers. item.title: ClickFix attackers using new tactic to evade detection, says Microsoft
item.description: Threat actors are trying a different tactic to sucker employees into falling for ClickFix phishing attacks that install malware, says Microsoft. Rather than asking potential victims to copy and paste a (malicious) command into the Run dialog, launched by hitting the Windows button plus the letter R, they are being told to use the Windows + X → I shortcut to launch Windows Terminal (wt.exe) directly.
